Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline. Let me explain. 5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot. But here's the thing — failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it. The reason? They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were. So we did what great teams do: we listened. We learned. We built. We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. Why we stopped billing by the hour — and never looked back. 🙌 When we started Fernway Studio, we did what every agency does: we charged hourly. And it changed everything. ✅ Clients know exactly what they're paying ✅ We're incentivized to work smarter, not longer ✅ Relationships are built on trust, not timesheets Since then, we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 went over our 6-week timeline. Pricing isn't just a number. It's a promise. 💯 Founders — how do you price your services? Let me know in the comments! #Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

We built a beautiful app. Nobody used it. 📱❌ When we launched Rotaship, we were so proud of our sleek, modern mobile app. We thought restaurant staff would love it. Reality check: only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month. 😳 That's when it hit us. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one. Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp. So in 2025, we made a tough call — we moved everything into WhatsApp. 💬 The results speak for themselves: ✅ 140 outlets ✅ Median reply time to shift messages: under 20 minutes The lesson? Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you. Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love. 💡 #ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

1,200 repositories. 🤯 When we launched Patchwork CI, we made a promise: always free for open source. Many people told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked. We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened. 👇 In September, we made one of the scariest decisions in Tabwise's history: increasing our price from $8 to $12 per user per month. 😰 Why? Because our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. We had a choice — compromise on quality, or charge what we're truly worth. We chose value. 💎 But we didn't want to leave our loyal customers behind. So every existing customer kept their $8 price for 12 months. 🤝 The result? Only 2 out of 140 customers churned in the following 2 months. TWO. The lesson: Your customers aren't paying for software. They're paying for outcomes. Don't be afraid to price accordingly. Hardware is hard. Here's our story. 🛠️ Our very first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact. 😞 As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are. We made the call to recall and replace every single one of those 400 labels — at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%. Because trust is everything. 🤝 We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. And since then? Zero contact failures across 6,000 labels. 🙌 Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does. To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again. 💪 #Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

Why we walked away from the 25% recruiting fee. 💼

For years, Northbound Talent did what every recruiting firm does: we charged 25% of first-year salary.

But something never sat right with me. 🤔

Our average fee was about $41,000 per hire. For an early-stage startup, that's a massive chunk of runway — and our incentives weren't aligned. Higher salary = bigger fee. Is that really partnership?

The result? We've placed 26 senior Rust engineers this year, and our relationships with clients have never been stronger. 🦀💪

It's time for the recruiting industry to evolve. Founders deserve better.
